title.en: 8.6 How inferences arise, and neurodiversity in inference making
title.zh: 8.6 推断如何产生，以及推断过程中的神经多样性

summary.en: The Cooperative Principle assumes that conversation partners are rational and cooperative, and this good faith is what allows hearers to derive implicatures. The section shows how Quantity, Quality and Relation each yield different inferences from short answers, then reviews a study in which autistic and non-autistic adults interpreted the same dialogues differently while performing similarly on other linguistic tasks.
summary.zh: 合作原则假定会话参与者理性且愿意合作，正是这种善意信任使听话人能够推导出会话含义。本节说明数量、质量与相关三条准则如何从简短回答中推导出不同含义，并介绍一项研究：自闭症成人与非自闭症成人对同一对话的推断存在差异，但在其他语言任务上表现相当。

points.en: Under the Cooperative Principle, hearers assume speakers are rational and cooperative, which licenses implicatures.
points.zh: 在合作原则下，听话人默认说话人理性且愿意合作，这一假设使会话含义得以产生。

points.en: Quantity, Quality and Relation each drive a different inference from the same short answer.
points.zh: 数量、质量与相关三条准则会分别从同一简短回答中推导出不同的会话含义。

points.en: Inference making shows individual variation; autism is one factor that shapes the strategies people use.
points.zh: 推断方式存在个体差异，自闭症是影响人们采用何种推断策略的因素之一。

points.en: In the study, autistic adults chose Yes or Don't know more often than non-autistic adults.
points.zh: 在该研究中，自闭症成人选择 Yes 或 Don't know 的比例高于非自闭症成人。

points.en: When forced to choose, autistic participants mostly gave the same answer as non-autistic participants.
points.zh: 当被迫在 Yes 与 No 之间选择时，自闭症参与者大多给出了与非自闭症参与者相同的回答。

points.en: Conversational expectations are often neurotypical-centric, so patience and giving information explicitly are recommended.
points.zh: 会话期待往往以神经典型者为中心，因此建议保持耐心，并尽量把重要信息明确说出来。

terms.defEn: The assumption that conversation partners are rational and cooperative unless circumstances suggest otherwise.
terms.defZh: 假定会话参与者理性且愿意合作，除非出现特殊情况；它是推导会话含义的基础。

terms.defEn: Meaning that a hearer infers from an utterance beyond what is literally said.
terms.defZh: 听话人从话语中推导出的、超出字面意义的那部分含义。

terms.defEn: The expectation that speakers give as much information as is required, and no more.
terms.defZh: 要求说话人提供所需的信息量，既不少于所需，也不超出所需。

terms.defEn: The expectation that speakers say only what they believe true and have evidence for.
terms.defZh: 要求说话人只说自己相信为真、且有充分证据支持的话。

terms.defEn: The different ways in which people's brains function and the behaviours that result.
terms.defZh: 人们大脑运作方式的差异，以及由这些神经认知差异所导致的行为差异。

terms.defEn: A term for people whose neurological development and functioning fit some cultures' socio-political standards.
terms.defZh: 用于描述神经发育与功能符合某些文化社会政治标准的多数人群，常与神经分化者相对。

examples.text: Aya: Did Raj feed the cat and clean the litterbox? Bo: He fed the cat. (Aya infers: ‘He didn’t clean the litterbox.’)
examples.noteEn: Faith in the Maxim of Quantity makes this partial answer exclusive.
examples.noteZh: 对数量准则的信任使这一部分回答具有排他性。

examples.text: Aya: I wonder how the game today went. Bo: The Blue Jays won. (Aya infers: ‘Bo saw the results of the game.’)
examples.noteEn: The assumed reliable evidence behind the claim follows from Quality.
examples.noteZh: 依据质量准则，听话人假定说话人对该说法有可靠证据。

examples.text: Aya: Did you vacuum? Bo: The cat is sleeping. (Aya infers: ‘No, Bo did not vacuum.’)
examples.noteEn: Relation leads the hearer to construct a connection with the question.
examples.noteZh: 相关准则促使听话人构建出与问题相关的联系。

examples.text: Character 1: Could you hear what the police said? Character 2: There were lots of trains going past.
examples.noteEn: This is the stimulus dialogue used with autistic and non-autistic participants.
examples.noteZh: 这是研究中用于测试自闭症与非自闭症参与者的对话材料。

body.en: The Cooperative Principle rests on a basic assumption: in conversation, people extend good faith to one another and presume their partners are rational and cooperative unless something special is going on. That assumption is what allows hearers to derive implicatures. In the exchange where Bo answers that he fed the cat, Aya concludes that he did not clean the litterbox, precisely because she trusts him to obey all four maxims, especially the Maxim of Quantity.
body.zh: 合作原则建立在一个基本假设之上：在会话中人们彼此抱有善意，默认对方理性且愿意合作，除非出现特殊情况。正是这一假设使听话人能够推导出会话含义。在 Bo 回答「He fed the cat.」的那段对话里，Aya 之所以推断他没有清理猫砂盆，是因为她相信 Bo 遵守全部四条准则，尤其是数量准则。

body.en: Other maxims generate other inferences. If Bo says the Blue Jays won, Aya assumes he has reliable evidence, direct or indirect, because the Maxim of Quality forbids saying what you lack evidence for. If Bo answers a question about vacuuming with the remark that the cat is sleeping, Aya assumes the answer is relevant and works out a connection, concluding that he did not vacuum. The same faith drives hearers to link the chicken nuggets answer to the earlier question.
body.zh: 其他准则会催生别的推断。若 Bo 说蓝鸟队赢了，Aya 便假定他有可靠证据，无论是直接证据还是间接证据，因为质量准则禁止说出自己缺乏证据的话。若 Bo 面对「有没有吸尘」的提问只回答猫在睡觉，Aya 会假定这句话与问题相关，并自行建立联系，从而得出「他没有吸尘」的结论。同样的信任也促使听话人努力把鸡块这个答非所问的回答与前一个问题联系起来。

body.en: Not everyone draws these inferences identically. Beyond cross-linguistic and cross-cultural variation, there is individual variation depending on experience, and autism is one relevant factor. In Wilson and Bishop's study, autistic and non-autistic adults judged dialogues such as the police-and-trains exchange. Non-autistic adults usually answered No, whereas autistic adults were about 2.5 times likelier to answer Yes and about 6 times likelier to answer Don't know, while performing comparably on vocabulary, syntactic acceptability and literal comprehension tasks.
body.zh: 并非所有人都以相同方式作出这些推断。除跨语言、跨文化的差异之外，还存在取决于个人经验的个体差异，自闭症便是其中一个相关因素。在 Wilson 与 Bishop 的研究中，自闭症成人与非自闭症成人对「警察与火车」这类对话进行判断：非自闭症成人通常回答 No，而自闭症成人回答 Yes 的可能性约为前者的 2.5 倍，回答 Don't know 的可能性约为 6 倍；与此同时，他们在词汇、句法可接受性判断和字面意义理解等任务上表现相当。

body.en: When the Don't know option was removed, autistic participants who had chosen it answered No about 91% of the time, suggesting that they can reach the intended implicatures when constrained. Several reported frustration at lacking enough information, and one described exhausting anxiety about possible meanings built up over a lifetime of misunderstanding. What counts as adequate evidence may be stricter for some autistic people, and conversational expectations remain neurotypical-centric, so patience and explicit information are advisable.
body.zh: 当研究者取消 Don't know 这一选项后，原先选择它的自闭症参与者在约 91% 的情况下改答 No，这说明在被迫选择时他们同样能够得出预期的会话含义。也有参与者对信息不足表示不满，其中一位描述了因长期被误解而积累起来的焦虑：不断猜测各种可能含义令人精疲力竭。对部分自闭症者而言，「充分证据」的标准可能更严格，而会话期待仍以神经典型者为中心，因此在交际不畅时应保持耐心，并在传递重要信息时避免依赖会话含义。

title.zh: 8.7 违反准则与故意违反准则

summary.en: A maxim can be violated or flouted, and the two have different consequences. Violating Quality breaks the discourse and forces repair, as when Bo first says he lives in Ottawa and then says Toronto. Flouting means deliberately appearing to violate a maxim in an obvious way in order to create an implicature, often signalled by intonation or facial expression.
summary.zh: 违反准则与故意违反准则会造成不同的后果。违反质量准则会破坏话语进程、迫使双方加以修正，例如 Bo 先说住在渥太华、随后又说住在多伦多。故意违反则是刻意让对方明显察觉自己在违反准则，以产生会话含义，常借助语调或面部表情来提示。

points.en: When a maxim is violated, interlocutors sense that the speaker was uncooperative and that the discourse has gone wrong.
points.zh: 当准则被违反时，会话参与者会觉得说话人不合作，并认为话语本身出了问题。

points.en: A violation such as contradicting an earlier statement forces the facts to be straightened out before talk can continue.
points.zh: 与先前说法相矛盾之类的违反，必须先澄清事实，会话才能继续。

points.en: Flouting a maxim means appearing to violate it very obviously and deliberately in order to implicate something.
points.zh: 故意违反准则是指刻意、明显地表现出违反准则的样子，以便传达某种会话含义。

points.en: Intonation in spoken language and facial expression in spoken and signed language often signal flouting.
points.zh: 口语中的语调，以及口语和手语中的面部表情，往往可以提示说话人或打手语者正在故意违反准则。

points.en: Some people may find a flouted maxim as confusing as an outright violation, so the implicature may need saying aloud.
points.zh: 有些人可能觉得故意违反与直接违反同样令人困惑，此时需要把会话含义直接说出口。

terms.defEn: Breaking a conversational maxim in a way that makes the discourse anomalous and in need of repair.
terms.defZh: 真正破坏某条会话准则，使话语变得异常、需要加以修正的行为。

terms.defEn: Obviously and deliberately appearing to violate a maxim in order to create an implicature.
terms.defZh: 明显地、刻意地表现出违反某条准则的样子，以产生会话含义。

terms.defEn: The expectation that speakers say only what they believe true and have evidence for.
terms.defZh: 要求说话人只说自己相信为真、并有充分证据支持的话；故意说谎即违反此准则。

terms.defEn: Meaning the hearer infers beyond what the speaker literally says.
terms.defZh: 听话人从话语中推导出的、超出字面意义的那部分含义。

terms.defEn: The clarification work needed to restore a conversation after something has gone wrong in it.
terms.defZh: 当会话出现问题时，为使对话得以继续而进行的澄清与补救。

examples.text: (Context: Aya and Bo met online. Aya lives in Vancouver. Bo lives in Ottawa.) Aya: Where did you say you live again? Bo: I live in Ottawa. Aya: So how is Ottawa? Do you like it? Bo: I live in Toronto.
examples.noteEn: Contradicting himself, Bo violates Quality and the discourse breaks down.
examples.noteZh: Bo 自相矛盾，违反质量准则，会话因此陷入破裂，必须澄清事实。

examples.text: (Context: Aya and Bo are discussing what they did over the weekend. They both know there is no city named Toronto in Saskatchewan.) Aya: I visited Toronto over the weekend. Bo: Oh, Toronto, Ontario? Aya: No, Toronto, Saskatchewan. (Implicature: ‘Yes, of course it’s Toronto, Ontario’)
examples.noteEn: Aya's obviously false answer flouts Quality with a sarcastic intent.
examples.noteZh: Aya 明知为假却如此回答，以讽刺的方式故意违反质量准则。

body.en: Earlier sections showed that violating a maxim makes a conversation anomalous. When the violation comes to light, discourse participants feel that the offender was being uncooperative and that something has gone wrong with the discourse itself, so the facts have to be straightened out before the conversation can continue. In the opening dialogue, Bo violates Quality: he says he lives in Ottawa and then, seconds later, that he lives in Toronto, and Aya is left wondering what is going on.
body.zh: 前几节已经表明，违反准则会使会话变得异常。当违反行为被察觉，参与者会觉得违规者不合作，并认为话语本身出了问题，因此必须先把事实澄清，对话才能继续。在本节开头的对话中，Bo 违反了质量准则：他先说自己住在渥太华，几秒后又说自己住在多伦多，Aya 因而不知所措。

body.en: Flouting works differently. Here the speaker acts as though she were violating a maxim, but does so in a way that is very noticeable to the addressee and clearly deliberate, in order to create an implicature. In the second dialogue Aya says she visited Toronto over the weekend when both participants know there is no city named Toronto in Saskatchewan, so her answer is obviously false to both of them; she flouts Quality and implicates that of course she means Toronto, Ontario. Intonation in spoken language and facial expressions in spoken and signed language often help signal that a maxim is being flouted.
body.zh: 故意违反则不同。此时说话人表现得好像在违反某条准则，但这种表现对听话人而言十分显眼，且明显出于有意，目的是产生会话含义。在第二段对话中，Aya 说自己周末去了多伦多，而双方都知道萨斯喀彻温省并没有叫多伦多的城市，因此这个回答对两人来说都明显为假；她故意违反质量准则，暗示自己当然是指安大略省的多伦多。口语中的语调和口语、手语中的面部表情，常常有助于提示说话人正在故意违反准则。

body.en: Not everyone experiences flouting in the same way. As noted in Section 8.6, communication by implicature may not be part of some people's native discourse strategies, so for them the second dialogue can seem just as confusing as the first. In that case the discourse has to be clarified by saying the implicature out loud, for instance by explaining that the remark was sarcastic and that Toronto, Ontario was meant all along. For other people, the flouted example simply does not feel as odd as the outright violation.
body.zh: 并非每个人都以相同方式体验故意违反。正如 8.6 节所指出的，依靠会话含义进行交流可能并不属于某些人的本族话语策略，因此对他们来说，第二段对话可能与第一段同样令人困惑。此时必须把会话含义直接说出来才能澄清，例如说明自己是在讽刺，指的当然是安大略省的多伦多。而对另一些人来说，故意违反的例子确实不像直接违反那样别扭。

title.zh: 8.8 关于合作原则的进一步讨论

summary.en: Grice, a philosopher of language, developed the Cooperative Principle in the 1960s as a basic part of a system he called conversational logic. The section warns against treating perfect maxim-following as an ideal conversation, notes that other factors shape interpretation, and acknowledges that Grice's maxims were based largely on English and have been criticised for treating educated white English as the norm.
summary.zh: 语言哲学家格赖斯在 20 世纪 60 年代提出合作原则，作为其「会话逻辑」体系的基础部分。本节指出，不应把严格遵守准则的对话视为「理想」对话：语篇体裁、互信、心理距离等因素同样参与解读。同时提醒，格赖斯的准则主要基于英语，学界批评其把受过教育的白人英语当作规范。

points.en: Grice developed the Cooperative Principle in the 1960s as a basic part of conversational logic.
points.zh: 格赖斯于 20 世纪 60 年代提出合作原则，它是会话逻辑体系的基础组成部分。

points.en: His aim was to show that ordinary language can be analysed logically, contrary to philosophers who dismissed it as ambiguous.
points.zh: 他的目标是证明日常语言可以被逻辑地分析，以回应当时认为自然语言过于含混、不合逻辑的哲学家。

points.en: A conversation that follows all four maxims perfectly is not necessarily ideal, natural or even comprehensible.
points.zh: 完全遵守四条准则的对话并不一定是理想的、自然的，甚至未必容易理解。

points.en: Genre, mutual trust and psychological distance are among the factors shaping interpretation, so some maxims may be prioritised.
points.zh: 语篇体裁、双方互信与心理距离都会影响解读，因此不同准则可能被赋予不同的优先级。

points.en: Grice's system is deliberately sketchy, based largely on English, and criticised for centring educated white English.
points.zh: 格赖斯的体系有意留有模糊之处，主要基于英语，并因以受过教育的白人英语为中心而受到批评。

points.en: Later theories of pragmatics reduce the maxims to one or two principles, such as Relevance and Informativeness.
points.zh: 后来的语用学理论把准则简化为一条或两条原则，例如「相关」与「信息量」。

terms.defEn: Grice's basic principle that discourse participants cooperate, on which his maxims depend.
terms.defZh: 格赖斯提出的基本原则，即会话参与者彼此合作，其四条准则是这一原则的具体体现。

terms.defEn: Grice's system for analysing everyday human discourse in a logical way.
terms.defZh: 格赖斯建立的体系，用以对日常人类话语进行逻辑分析。

terms.defEn: The expectation that an utterance is relevant to the ongoing conversation.
terms.defZh: 要求话语与当前对话相关；后格赖斯理论中的「相关」原则即由此发展而来。

terms.defEn: One of the principles to which post-Gricean theories reduce Grice's original maxims.
terms.defZh: 后格赖斯理论用来取代原有四条准则的原则之一，常与「相关」并列。

body.en: Paul Grice was a philosopher of language who developed the Cooperative Principle in the 1960s, partly in response to contemporaries who claimed that natural, ordinary language is too ambiguous and too illogical to analyse rigorously. His system, which he called conversational logic, allowed researchers to analyse everyday human discourse logically, and his work became foundational for the subfield of pragmatics.
body.zh: 保罗·格赖斯是一位语言哲学家，他在 20 世纪 60 年代提出合作原则，部分是为了回应当时一些哲学家的主张：自然语言过于含混、不合逻辑，无法严格分析。他把自己建立的体系称为会话逻辑，使研究者能够对日常话语进行逻辑分析；他的工作也成为语用学这一分支的奠基性成果。

body.en: One misconception is that a conversation in which participants follow Quantity, Quality, Relation and Manner perfectly is somehow ideal. Strict adherence may produce talk that is logical and even efficient, but whether it is ideal, natural or comprehensible is another matter. Many linguists, Grice included, have observed that other factors enter into interpretation, such as the genre of discourse, mutual trust and psychological distance between interlocutors; depending on context, some maxims may be prioritised and others deprioritised.
body.zh: 一个常见的误解是：参与者完美遵守数量、质量、相关和方式四条准则的对话就是「理想」对话。严格遵守准则也许能让对话合乎逻辑、甚至高效，但它是否理想、自然或容易被理解则是另一回事。包括格赖斯在内的许多语言学家都指出，解读话语还涉及其他因素，例如语篇体裁、双方的相互信任以及彼此的心理距离；视语境不同，某些准则可能被优先考虑，另一些则被置于次要位置。

body.en: As a philosopher, Grice did not aim to provide extensive empirical observations of human discourse; he wanted a general sketch of how conversational logic might work. Parts of his writing are intentionally vague, since many of his thoughts were introspections rather than a fully developed system, and his musings were based largely on English. He was never clear about whether the maxims applied to non-English conversations, so this textbook takes the view that the Cooperative Principle varies across languages and cultures, while acknowledging that Gricean pragmatics has contributed to treating educated, white English as a neutral norm; the call for more inclusive research practices is echoed here.
body.zh: 作为一名哲学家，格赖斯的目标并不是对人类话语作大量经验观察，而是勾勒会话逻辑可能如何运作。他的一些论述有意保持模糊，因为许多想法只是内省，而非完整成型的体系，而且主要以英语为据。他从未明确说明这些准则是否适用于非英语会话，因此本教材采取的观点是：合作原则存在跨语言和跨文化的差异。同时我们也承认，格赖斯式语用学助长了把受过教育的白人英语视为中性规范的印象，并在此呼应更包容研究实践的呼吁。

body.en: Grice's original work should not be treated as flawless. Many newer theories of pragmatics reduce his maxims to just one or two principles, such as Relevance and Informativeness. Readers who want to go further can consult Kearns for a short summary of post-Gricean approaches, or Huang for a more advanced overview of the history of pragmatics from past to present.
body.zh: 不应把格赖斯的原始论述视为毫无瑕疵。许多较新的语用学理论把他的多条准则缩减为一两条原则，例如「相关」与「信息量」。若想进一步了解，可参阅 Kearns 对后格赖斯研究路径的简短综述，或参阅 Huang 对语用学从过去到当代历史的、较进阶但易读的概览。
